claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The equiatomic disordered-BCC alloy has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The alloy has limited plasticity associated with its high Mo content.
Annealing at approximately 700°C for 4–8 hours can induce short-range ordering in NbZrTiHfMo.
Approximately 700°C is well below the recrystallization threshold of this alloy.
Keeping the anneal below the recrystallization threshold will avoid grain coarsening and unwanted precipitation.
The annealing treatment will form localized short-range-order clusters that modify the local chemical environment.
Short-range-order clusters reduce extremes in local electronegativity differences caused by Mo.
Moderating local chemical fluctuations eases dislocation motion.
Short-range ordering enables more slip systems in this alloy.
The annealing-induced short-range ordering maintains solid-solution strengthening.
Maintaining solid-solution strengthening preserves the alloy's high compressive yield strength.
After treatment, the alloy will retain a room-temperature compressive yield strength of around 1700 MPa.
After treatment, the alloy will exhibit significantly greater room-temperature compressive plastic strain than the as-cast disordered alloy.
Annealing above 700°C or substantially longer than 8 hours may cause microstructural changes that negate the proposed benefits.
The degree of short-range ordering required to optimize strength and plasticity is governed in part by complex diffusion kinetics in refractory high-entropy alloys.
